dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: Well, it all goes back to Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: I was making a living by doing some menial labor at Dornman Port before all this. And then I ran into people from the Kanjou Commission who were recruiting sailors.

dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: Their supervisor told me that it wouldn't be a tiring gig and that it paid well. I could even travel to Inazuma!

dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: Back when we were all locked down, regular people couldn't come to Inazuma at all. Only cargo ships affiliated with the Kanjou Commission could pass through.

dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: I figured that it might be a good job since I could visit the outside world and make some money. That's why I boarded the ship with them.

dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: But the moment I got there, I was stuck in Ritou, and had to do all kinds of hard, exhausting labor!

dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: So you bet your last Mora that the moment the Sakoku Decree was abolished, I was on the first ship back home.

dialogues.speaker: Jones
dialogues.text: Thank you, Lord Barbatos, for blowing the winds of freedom toward Inazuma...
